mainTopic: The end of the dispute about a half-slave, half-free man (חציו עבד וחציו בן חורין), and a new משנה about a slave sent to slaughter his master's קרבן פסח who does not know or forgets which animal to use.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the משנה about a man who is half slave and half free. בית שמאי argue that he cannot marry anyone, and the world was created for פריה ורביה. So for תיקון העולם his master is forced to free him, and בית הלל change their ruling to agree. A new משנה follows about a slave sent to slaughter his master's קרבן פסח. If the master named no animal, whatever the slave brings is fine, and if he brings two, the master eats from the first. If the slave forgot a specific instruction, he slaughters both animals with a condition. If the master also forgot, both are burned, but they are exempt from פסח שני. The גמרא explains that eating from the first fits people like a king and queen, who are not particular. It supports this with a ברייתא about רבן גמליאל, which also tells a story about a lizard found in the royal kitchen. אביי shows how a slave can own an animal, and he limits the exemption from פסח שני to forgetting after זריקה. Some place this limit on a ברייתא about five mixed-up hides instead. The גמרא then asks why all five owners are exempt, rejects several possible fixes, and begins rejecting a conditional פסח/שלמים offering, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בית שמאי object that the half-slave cannot marry anyone
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי attack בית הלל's arrangement. It protects the master but leaves the half-slave unable to marry a שפחה or a free woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: You fixed things for his master, but you did not fix things for him. He cannot marry a maidservant, because half of him is already free. He cannot marry a free woman, because half of him is still a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי are objecting to בית הלל's ruling that the half-slave works one day for his master and one day for himself. They point out that this leaves the man himself stuck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's solution looks after the master's financial rights. בית שמאי say it ignores the man's personal life. His free half forbids him from marrying a שפחה, and his slave half forbids him from marrying a free Jewish woman. That means no marriage is possible for him at all.

keyTerms.meaning: half of him is a slave

steps.confusionAlert: This is still the words of the משנה, spoken by בית שמאי. It is not the גמרא asking a question.

phrases.english: You have fixed things for his master,
but for himself you have not fixed things.
To marry a maidservant he cannot —
because half of him is already free,
to marry a free woman he cannot —
because half of him is still a slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּקַּנְתֶּם אֶת רַבּוֹ, וְאֶת עַצְמוֹ לֹא תִּקַּנְתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues בית שמאי's response to בית הלל's ruling from the earlier part of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's arrangement of alternating workdays between master and self.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The arrangement leaves the half-slave with no permitted marriage partner, so it fails to solve his real problem.

steps.title: He cannot simply stay unmarried
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי reject the option that he should just not marry, because the world was created for having children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should he just stay idle and not marry? But the world was created only for having children, as the verse says: "He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in."
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי anticipate a possible answer: maybe the man should just remain unmarried. They reject this using a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say the marriage problem doesn't matter, because he can simply stay single. בית שמאי respond that פריה ורביה is the purpose of creation itself, as ישעיהו says the world was formed "to be inhabited." So leaving him unable to marry is not an acceptable outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: he should be idle (refrain from marrying)
He did not create it to be empty
He formed it to be inhabited

steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק ("לשבת יצרה") is the classic source showing that populating the world is a basic value. It is used elsewhere in halacha as well.

phrases.english: Should he remain idle (and not marry)?
But was the world not created
only for having children,
as it says: "He did not create it to be empty,
(rather) He formed it to be inhabited."

steps.triggerLanguage: יִבְטַל, וַהֲלֹא לֹא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם אֶלָּא לִפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off the possible escape from step 1's problem, namely that he simply not marry.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested option that the half-slave should simply remain unmarried.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against פריה ורביה, which is the very purpose of the world's creation.

steps.title: בית שמאי's solution: force the master to free him
steps.stepSummary: Because of תיקון העולם, the master is forced to free the man fully, and the man writes a שטר for half his value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, to set the world right, we force his master to make him a free man, and the slave writes a document owing half of his value.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי now give their own ruling, which solves both people's problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Full freedom lets the man marry a free Jewish woman. The master does not lose money, because the freed man writes a שטר promising to pay the half of his value that the master still owned. This protects both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: setting the world right; a rule made for the general good

phrases.english: Rather, for the sake of setting the world right,
we force his master
and he makes him a free man,
and he (the slave) writes a document for half his value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִפְּנֵי תִּיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם כּוֹפִין אֶת רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the positive solution after steps 1 and 2 showed the problem.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court compels the master to free the half-slave fully, and the freed man owes the master half his value by a written שטר.

steps.title: בית הלל change their ruling to follow בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל retract their position and rule like בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל went back and ruled like בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends the dispute: בית הלל accept בית שמאי's argument and change their ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the halacha follows בית הלל. Here בית הלל themselves were convinced and switched sides. So the final halacha is בית שמאי's ruling: force the master to free him, and the man writes a שטר.
steps.whatToRemember: For a half-slave, half-free man, the final halacha is that the master is forced to free him for תיקון העולם, and the man owes half his value. בית הלל agreed to this.
steps.confusionAlert: This is one of the rare cases where the halacha follows בית שמאי. It is not because בית שמאי won a vote. It is because בית הלל themselves changed their minds.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel went back
to rule like Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזְרוּ בֵּית הִילֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute in favor of step 3's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows בית שמאי: the half-slave is freed by compulsion and writes a שטר for half his value.

steps.title: New משנה: a slave sent to slaughter the פסח without instructions
steps.stepSummary: A master tells his slave to slaughter the קרבן פסח without naming an animal. A גדי or a טלה are both fine. If the slave slaughters both, the master eats from the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says to his slave, "Go and slaughter the פסח for me": if he slaughtered a young goat, the master may eat it. If he slaughtered a lamb, the master may eat it. If he slaughtered a goat and a lamb, the master eats from the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a fresh case. It deals with a master who sent his slave to slaughter his קרבן פסח without saying which kind of animal to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן פסח can be either a goat or a sheep, so whichever the slave picks is valid. If he slaughters both, the master can only be registered on one קרבן פסח. Since he left the choice to the slave, he is counted on the first one slaughtered. The second one cannot be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: "Eat from the first" means the master is counted only on the first animal slaughtered. It does not mean he eats some of each.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who says to his slave:
Go and slaughter the Paschal offering for me,
if he slaughtered a kid — he (the master) may eat,
if he slaughtered a lamb — he may eat,
if he slaughtered a kid and a lamb —
he eats from the first one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לְעַבְדּוֹ צֵא וּשְׁחוֹט עָלַי אֶת הַפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic after the half-slave discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified instruction allows either a goat or a lamb. If both are slaughtered, the master is registered on the first.

steps.title: What if the slave forgot what his master told him?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what the slave should do if the master did name an animal but the slave forgot which one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he forgot what his master told him, what should he do?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה raises a new version of the case. Here the master gave a specific instruction, but the slave forgot it. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This differs from step 5. There, the master left the choice open. Here, the master chose a specific animal, so slaughtering the wrong kind would not count for him.

phrases.english: If he forgot what his master told him,
how should he act?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁכַח מָה אָמַר לוֹ רַבּוֹ, כֵּיצַד יַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the case from step 5 to a situation where the master did specify an animal but the slave forgot which.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the slave can fulfill a specific instruction that he no longer remembers.

steps.title: Slaughter both animals with a conditional statement
steps.stepSummary: The slave slaughters both animals and states a condition. Whichever animal the master named belongs to the master, and the other belongs to the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should slaughter a lamb and a kid and say: "If my master told me a kid, the kid is his and the lamb is mine. If my master told me a lamb, the lamb is his and the kid is mine."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question by giving the slave a conditional formula. This way each animal ends up assigned to the right person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slave does not know which animal the master meant, so he covers both possibilities. Once the master later says what he had instructed, it becomes clear which animal was his. The other animal counts as the slave's own קרבן פסח.
steps.whatToRemember: With no specific instruction, any valid animal works, and if two are slaughtered, the first counts. With a forgotten specific instruction, the slave slaughters both and uses a condition so that each animal goes to the correct owner.

phrases.english: He should slaughter a lamb and a kid, and say:
If my master told me a kid —
the kid is his and the lamb is mine,
and if my master told me a lamb —
the lamb is his and the kid is mine.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִשְׁחַט טָלֶה וּגְדִי, וְיֹאמַר: אִם גְּדִי אֲמַר לִי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Slaughter both animals with a stipulation assigning the master's named animal to him and the other to the slave.

steps.title: When the master also forgot, both animals are burned
steps.stepSummary: If the master also forgot which animal he named, both animals go to שריפה, but master and עבד are exempt from פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his master also forgot what he told him, both animals go out to the place of burning. They are exempt from bringing פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its case. Now nobody remembers which animal the master named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עבד's condition from Step 7 only works if someone can later identify which animal belongs to the master. If the master also forgot, no one can know who is registered on which animal, so neither may be eaten and both are burned. Even so, the משנה exempts them from פסח שני. Whether this depends on when the master forgot (before or after the blood was sprinkled) is discussed by אביי in Steps 20–25.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where disqualified קדשים are burned
The make-up פסח offering brought one month later

steps.whatToRemember: An animal that cannot be eaten does not mean the מצוה failed. If the blood was offered properly, the obligation is done, even if the meat must be burned.
steps.confusionAlert: Burning the animals does not mean the קרבן פסח was invalid. The burning is only because nobody can know who may eat which animal. The exemption from פסח שני shows that the obligation still counts as fulfilled.

phrases.english: If his master forgot what he had told him,
both of them go out to the place of burning,
and they are exempt from offering the second Pesach.
phrases.notes: אביי later limits this to forgetting after the blood was sprinkled, according to one version (Steps 20–25).

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁכַח רַבּוֹ מָה אָמַר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the forgetting case from the עבד alone to both the עבד and the master.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If both forgot, both animals are burned, but the master and עבד are exempt from פסח שני.

steps.title: Isn't the first ruling of the משנה obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה needed to teach that an unspecified animal is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why the משנה needed to teach the ruling from Step 5. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if the master did not name an animal, whatever the עבד slaughters is fine. The גמרא objects that this is obvious: if the master gave no instructions, he clearly does not care which animal is used.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
It is obvious. This asks why something needed to be taught at all.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It is obvious!
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's ruling that whatever the slave slaughters is acceptable.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא and questions the need for the ruling in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that if the master did not specify, either animal is acceptable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the master gave no instruction, he clearly has no preference, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The master's habit does not count as an instruction
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a master who usually uses the other animal: even so, he may eat what the עבד slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the עבד slaughtered a kid, the master eats it, even though he usually uses a lamb. If the עבד slaughtered a lamb, the master eats it, even though he usually uses a kid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's ruling is not obvious. It teaches something new about a master who has a usual habit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a master who always uses a lamb silently meant a lamb, so a kid would not count for him. The משנה teaches that a habit is not an instruction. Since he did not say anything, he accepts whatever the עבד brings.
steps.whyThisMatters: A person's usual habit is not treated as an unspoken condition when he gave open-ended instructions.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered a kid, he (the master) may eat it,
even though he is used to a lamb.
If he slaughtered a lamb, he may eat it,
even though he is used to a kid.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט גְּדִי יֹאכַל אַף עַל גַּב דִּרְגִיל בְּטָלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' objection by narrowing the משנה to a master with a usual habit.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing: the משנה speaks about a master with an established habit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A master's habit might be treated as a silent instruction, so the other animal would not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: A habit is not an instruction. Whatever the עבד slaughters is acceptable.

steps.title: How can the master be registered on two animals?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lets the master eat from the first of two animals, but a ברייתא forbids being registered on two קרבנות פסח at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he slaughtered a kid and a lamb, the master eats from the first one. But a ברייתא teaches that one may not be registered on two Pesach offerings at once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and challenges it with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the master to eat from whichever animal came first, he must have been registered on both animals in advance. That directly contradicts the ברייתא, which forbids registering on two קרבנות פסח together.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (in a ברייתא)! This introduces a contradicting source.
Registered as a participant on a קרבן פסח

phrases.english: If he slaughtered a kid and a lamb,
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: he eats from the first one.
But wasn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נִמְנִין עַל שְׁנֵי פְסָחִים כְּאֶחָד!
phrases.english: One may not be registered on two Pesach offerings at once!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַנְיָא אֵין נִמְנִין עַל שְׁנֵי פְסָחִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the next line of the משנה and challenges it with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the master eats from the first of two animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating from either animal implies he was registered on both, which the ברייתא forbids.

steps.title: The משנה is about a king and queen
steps.stepSummary: The משנה refers to people like a king and queen, who are not particular and are registered only on whichever animal is slaughtered first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is speaking about a king and queen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying what kind of master the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king and queen do not care which animal their servants prepare, since everything they are served is of fine quality. So from the start, they intend to be registered only on whichever animal is slaughtered first. They are never registered on two animals at once, and the ברייתא is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: A king and queen. These represent people who are not particular about which food they are served.

steps.whatToRemember: There is no contradiction: the master is registered on only one animal, the first one slaughtered. This works because he is someone who is not particular, like a king and queen.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer is NOT that kings are allowed to be registered on two קרבנות פסח. They are registered on only one, the first, so the rule of the ברייתא stays fully in place.

phrases.english: Our mishna is speaking of a king and queen.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין בְּמֶלֶךְ וּמַלְכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from the ברייתא by narrowing the משנה to a specific kind of master.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing: the משנה refers to masters who are not particular.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The master was registered on both animals, which contradicts the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The master intended from the start to be registered only on whichever animal is slaughtered first, so he is registered on just one.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a king and queen with two פסחים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the king-and-queen answer with a ברייתא. The ברייתא states that one may not register on two פסחים at once, then tells of royal servants who slaughtered two פסחים. The question was passed from king to queen to רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: One may not be registered on two פסחים at once. There was a story with a king and queen. They told their servants: 'Go and slaughter the פסח for us.' The servants went and slaughtered two פסחים for them. The servants came and asked the king which one to use. He told them: 'Go ask the queen.' They came and asked the queen. She told them: 'Go ask רבן גמליאל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the answer it just gave about the king and queen. This step only sets up the story; the decisive ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens with the same rule that caused the problem in Step 11: no one may be registered on two פסחים at once. It then describes exactly the kind of case Step 12 described: royalty, two animals, and servants unsure which to use. Because the ברייתא states the rule and the royal case side by side, it shows that this case is a known exception.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it was taught in a ברייתא.' Here it brings support, not a challenge.
Being registered (signed up) on a קרבן פסח
At once, at the same time
An incident or story used as a source for halacha
The נשיא, head of the סנהדרין, whom the royal court asked for rulings

steps.confusionAlert: The word וְהָתַנְיָא usually opens a challenge ('But it was taught...'). Here it does the opposite. It brings a ברייתא that SUPPORTS the answer from Step 12. Read it as 'and so it was taught.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the idea in Step 12. Being registered on two פסחים is normally forbidden, but people who don't care which animal is used are counted only on the first one slaughtered.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין נִמְנִין עַל שְׁנֵי פְסָחִים כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: And it was taught: One may not register on two Paschal offerings at once,
phrases.notes: The general rule, the same one quoted in Step 11

phrases.english: and there was an incident with a king and queen
phrases.notes: The story that shows the exception

phrases.english: who said to their servants:
Go out and slaughter the Paschal offering for us,
phrases.notes: They did not say which animal to use

phrases.english: and they went out and slaughtered two Paschal offerings for them.
phrases.notes: Each servant (or group) slaughtered a different animal

phrases.english: They came and asked the king,
phrases.notes: Which one should be eaten?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: לְכוּ וְשַׁאֲלוּ אֶת הַמַּלְכָּה.
phrases.english: he said to them: Go and ask the queen.
They came and asked the queen,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לָהֶם: לְכוּ וְשַׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: she said to them: Go and ask Rabban Gamliel.
phrases.notes: The question goes to the halachic authority

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין נִמְנִין עַל שְׁנֵי פְסָחִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting the answer in Step 12 that the משנה speaks about royalty who are not particular.
steps.raayaObject: The answer in Step 12: people who are not particular are registered only on the first animal slaughtered, so they may eat from it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording an incident with a king, queen and רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל rules: royalty eat from the first, we eat from neither
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל rules that a king and queen, who are not particular, may eat from the first פסח slaughtered. Ordinary people, who are particular, could eat from neither animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came and asked רבן גמליאל. He told them: 'A queen and king, who are easygoing about such things, should eat from the first one. But we would not eat from the first or from the second.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל gives the ruling that proves the גמרא's answer from Step 12. Royalty may eat from the first animal, but regular people could not eat from either one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king and queen let their servants pick whatever they want, so they are counted only on the first animal slaughtered. They were never really registered on two, and the first one is theirs. Ordinary people care which animal is used, so they do not hand that choice to the servants. With two animals slaughtered for them, they would be registered on both at once, which the ברייתא forbids, so they could eat from neither. This matches Step 12 exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: They are easygoing; they don't mind which one is chosen for them
The first one (the animal slaughtered first)

steps.confusionAlert: 'דעתן קלה' here is NOT an insult meaning 'light-headed.' It means royalty have so much that they don't care which animal is served to them. That is why they are counted only on the first one.
steps.whatToRemember: Royalty, who are not particular, may eat from the first פסח slaughtered for them. Ordinary people, who are particular, may eat from neither, because they cannot be registered on two פסחים at once.

phrases.english: They came and asked Rabban Gamliel,
he said to them:
A queen and king, who are easygoing about it —
phrases.notes: They accept whatever their servants choose

phrases.english: should eat from the first one.
phrases.notes: They are counted only on the first animal slaughtered

phrases.english: We would not eat
phrases.notes: Ordinary people, who are particular

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא מִן הַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.english: neither from the first nor from the second.
phrases.notes: Because one may not be registered on two at once

steps.triggerLanguage: מַלְכָּה וּמֶלֶךְ דְּדַעְתָּן קַלָּה עֲלֵיהֶן — יֹאכְלוּ מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first story in the ברייתא with רבן גמליאל's ruling, which proves the answer in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The answer in Step 12 that our משנה speaks about people who are not particular.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן גמליאל's ruling in the ברייתא: royalty eat from the first, ordinary people eat from neither.

steps.title: A second story: a lizard found in the royal kitchen
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells a second story about the same royal household. A lizard was found in the kitchen, and people wanted to declare the whole meal טמא. Again the question went from king to queen to רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time, a lizard was found in the kitchen, and they wanted to declare the entire meal טמא. They came and asked the king. He told them: 'Go ask the queen.' They came and asked the queen. She told them: 'Go ask רבן גמליאל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to a second, unrelated story involving the same king, queen and רבן גמליאל. This step only sets up the question; the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lizard is one of the שרצים, and a dead שרץ makes food it touches טמא. Since it was found in the kitchen, everyone assumed it was dead and had made the whole meal טמא. The ברייתא includes this story because it is part of the same collection of incidents, not to prove anything about קרבן פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: A lizard, one of the eight שרצים whose dead bodies are טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Here בֵּית הַמִּטְבָּחַיִם means the kitchen, not a slaughterhouse.

phrases.english: And another time
phrases.notes: A second incident in the same ברייתא

phrases.english: a lizard was found in the kitchen
and they wanted to declare the entire meal impure.
phrases.notes: They assumed the lizard was dead

phrases.english: They came and asked the king,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: לְכוּ וְשַׁאֲלוּ אֶת הַמַּלְכָּה.
phrases.english: he said to them: Go and ask the queen.
They came and asked the queen,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לָהֶם: לְכוּ וְשַׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: she said to them: Go and ask Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשׁוּב פַּעַם אַחַת נִמְצֵאת הַלְטָאָה בְּבֵית הַמִּטְבָּחַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues with a second incident involving the same people, on a different topic (טומאה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a lizard found in the kitchen seemed to make the whole meal טמא, and the question was brought to רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: Cold water shows the lizard is alive, so the meal is טהור
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל asked whether the kitchen was hot. Since it was, he had cold water poured on the lizard. It moved, showing it was alive, so he declared the entire meal טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came and asked him. He said to them: 'Is the kitchen hot or cold?' They told him: 'Hot.' He said to them: 'Go pour a cup of cold water on it.' They went and poured a cup of cold water on it, and it moved. So רבן גמליאל declared the entire meal טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל tests whether the lizard is really dead. When it moves, he declares the whole meal טהור. This ends the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a hot kitchen, a lizard might only be stunned by the heat and look dead. Cold water can wake it up. Once it moved, it was clearly alive, and only a dead שרץ makes things טמא. So nothing became טמא and the meal was permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: A living שרץ does not make food טמא. רבן גמליאל checked with cold water, the lizard moved, and the whole royal meal was declared טהור.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows that a halachic authority should check the facts before declaring something טמא, instead of assuming the worst.

phrases.english: They came and asked him,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: בֵּית הַמִּטְבָּחַיִם רוֹתֵחַ אוֹ צוֹנֵן?
phrases.english: he said to them: Is the kitchen hot or cold?
phrases.notes: Heat can stun a lizard so that it only looks dead

phrases.english: They said to him: Hot.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: לְכוּ וְהָטִילוּ עָלֶיהָ כּוֹס שֶׁל צוֹנֵן.
phrases.english: He said to them: Go and pour a cup of cold water on it.
phrases.notes: A test to see if it is still alive

phrases.aramaic: הָלְכוּ וְהֵטִילוּ עָלֶיהָ כּוֹס שֶׁל צוֹנֵן וְרִיחֲשָׁה,
phrases.english: They went and poured a cup of cold water on it, and it moved,
phrases.notes: Proof that it was alive

phrases.aramaic: וְטִהֵר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל כׇּל הַסְּעוּדָה כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: and Rabban Gamliel declared the entire meal pure.
phrases.notes: A living שרץ does not make things טמא

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית הַמִּטְבָּחַיִם רוֹתֵחַ אוֹ צוֹנֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the lizard question set up in Step 15 with רבן גמליאל's test and ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The lizard was alive, and a living שרץ does not make things טמא, so the entire meal was declared טהור.

steps.title: The whole royal meal depended on רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the lizard story with a comment: the king relied on the queen, the queen relied on רבן גמליאל, so the entire meal depended on רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out the king depended on the queen, and the queen depended on רבן גמליאל. So the entire meal depended on רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a closing remark to the story of the lizard. It points out that everything came down to רבן גמליאל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person in the chain passed the question up: the servants to the king, the king to the queen, the queen to רבן גמליאל. His ruling of טהור saved the whole meal. This line ends the ברייתא's stories and adds no new law.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out / it comes out that

phrases.english: It turns out the king is dependent on the queen,
and it turns out the queen is dependent on Rabban Gamliel,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאת כׇּל הַסְּעוּדָה תְּלוּיָה בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: so it turns out the entire meal is dependent on Rabban Gamliel.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's stories about the royal household end here. Next, the גמרא goes back to the משנה about the slave.
steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא מֶלֶךְ תָּלוּי בַּמַּלְכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closing comment on the lizard story from step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The fate of the whole royal meal rested on רבן גמליאל's ruling.

steps.title: How can a slave say 'this one is mine'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the slave who forgot his master's instructions and says one animal is 'mine'. It asks how this works, since whatever a slave acquires belongs to his master.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He forgot what his master told him, etc.', so he says one animal is for his master and the other is 'mine'. But how can it be 'mine'? Whatever a slave acquires, his master acquires!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה. It challenges the slave's statement that one of the two animals belongs to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the slave brings a lamb and a kid. He says: whichever one my master asked for is his, and the other is mine. But a slave cannot own property, because anything he gets automatically goes to his master. So how can the slave own a separate פסח?

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever a slave acquires, his master acquires
Etc. (the quote of the משנה continues)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the slave's right to eat a פסח. It is about ownership: the slave cannot own the animal, so it would really be the master's too.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁכַח מַה שֶּׁאָמַר לוֹ רַבּוֹ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: (The mishna said:) He forgot what his master told him, etc.
phrases.notes: Quotation from the משנה

phrases.english: "Mine"?!
Whatever a slave acquires, his master acquires!

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלִּי?! מַה שֶּׁקָּנָה עֶבֶד קָנָה רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the ברייתא's stories to a new line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The slave's statement in the משנה that the second animal is 'mine'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A slave cannot own property, so the animal could never really be his own.

steps.title: A shepherd gives the slave an animal that the master cannot claim
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains how the slave can own the animal. He goes to a shepherd his master regularly deals with. The shepherd gives him an animal on the condition that the master has no rights in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The slave goes to a shepherd his master usually buys from. That shepherd is happy to help solve his master's problem. He gives the slave one of the animals on the condition that the master has no rights in it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 18. He shows a way for the slave to truly own one animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a slave's property goes to his master can be avoided. This works when the giver says the master has no rights in the gift. The shepherd agrees because he is a regular supplier and wants to help his customer. So the slave really does own one animal, and his condition can work.

keyTerms.meaning: He is pleased / it suits him

keyTerms.term: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לְרַבּוֹ רְשׁוּת בּוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: On condition that his master has no rights in it

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a general tool: a gift can be given to a slave in a way that keeps it out of the master's ownership.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹלֵךְ אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה הָרָגִיל רַבּוֹ אֶצְלוֹ,
phrases.english: He goes to a shepherd whom his master regularly deals with,
who is pleased to provide a solution for his master,
and he transfers to him one of them

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לְרַבּוֹ רְשׁוּת בּוֹ.
phrases.english: on condition that his master has no rights to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הוֹלֵךְ אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה הָרָגִיל רַבּוֹ אֶצְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical mechanism (defines how the case is set up)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything the slave has automatically belongs to his master, so he cannot own a separate animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: A gift given on condition that the master has no rights in it stays the slave's own.

steps.title: The exemption from פסח שני applies only if they forgot after the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case where the master also forgot, and both are exempt from פסח שני. אביי limits this to forgetting after the blood was sprinkled, because at that moment the offering was still fit to be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'His master forgot what he told him, etc.' אביי said: This was taught only when he forgot after the sprinkling. At the time the blood was sprinkled, the offering was fit to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. אביי narrows the משנה's ruling that master and slave are exempt from פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is the moment of זריקה, the sprinkling of the blood. If they still knew which animal was the master's at that time, each animal was a valid פסח fit to be eaten. Forgetting afterward means both are burned. But the מצוה was already done, so no פסח שני is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when (limits the case)
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: שָׁכַח רַבּוֹ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר לוֹ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: (The mishna said:) His master forgot what he told him, etc.
phrases.notes: Quotation from the משנה

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁכַח אַחַר זְרִיקָה,
phrases.english: They taught this only where he forgot after the sprinkling,
for at the time the blood was sprinkled
it was fit to be eaten.

steps.confusionAlert: Being burned later does not cancel the מצוה. What matters is whether the animal was fit to be eaten at the moment of זריקה.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁכַח אַחַר זְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption from פסח שני applies only when they forgot after זריקה, since at זריקה the offering was fit to be eaten.

steps.title: If they forgot before the sprinkling, they must bring פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the opposite case. If the forgetting happened before the sprinkling, the offering was not fit to be eaten at זריקה, so they must bring פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he forgot before the sprinkling, then when the blood was sprinkled the offering was not fit to be eaten. So they must bring פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his statement with the contrasting case. This shows exactly where the משנה's exemption stops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no one knew which animal belonged to whom when the blood was sprinkled, neither animal could be eaten at that moment. A פסח that is unfit to be eaten at זריקה does not count. So master and slave never fulfilled their מצוה, and they must bring פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: The second פסח, brought a month later by those who missed the first

steps.whatToRemember: The key moment is זריקה. If they forgot after it, they are exempt from פסח שני. If they forgot before it, they must bring פסח שני.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a פסח counts only if it is fit to be eaten when its blood is sprinkled.

phrases.english: But if he forgot before the sprinkling,
so that when the blood was sprinkled
it was not fit to be eaten,
they are obligated to perform the second Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל שָׁכַח לִפְנֵי זְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's statement from step 20 with the opposite case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Forgetting before זריקה makes the פסח invalid, so both master and slave must bring פסח שני.

steps.title: A second version: the five mixed-up hides
steps.stepSummary: Some place אביי's rule on a ברייתא. Five פסח hides got mixed up and one had a wart. All the meat is burned, but all five owners are exempt from פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach אביי's statement on a ברייתא instead. Five people's פסח hides got mixed together, and a wart was found on one of them. All the meat goes out to be burned, but all five are exempt from bringing פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says some people taught אביי's rule on a different source, a ברייתא. It quotes that ברייתא here to set up אביי's comment, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wart is a blemish that makes a קרבן unfit. Nobody knows which lamb the blemished hide came from, so all five lambs must be burned. Even so, the ברייתא says all five owners are exempt from פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (a second version of where a statement was said)
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
A wart, a blemish that makes an animal unfit to be a קרבן
The place where unfit קדשים are burned

steps.confusionAlert: Only the hides got mixed up, not the meat itself. That is why nobody can tell which lamb was the blemished one.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on a baraita:
phrases.notes: "It" refers to אביי's statement from the previous steps.

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ עוֹרוֹת פִּסְחֵיהֶן זֶה בָּזֶה,
phrases.english: Five people whose Pesach lambs' hides got mixed up with each other,
and a wart was found on one of them —
phrases.notes: The wart is a blemish, so one of the lambs was unfit.

phrases.english: all of them go out to the place of burning,
phrases.notes: Each lamb might be the blemished one, so none can be eaten.

phrases.english: and they are exempt from doing the second Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַבָּרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of where אביי's rule from Steps 20-21 was originally said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five פסח hides got mixed and one had a wart. All the meat is burned, but the owners are exempt from פסח שני.

steps.title: אביי limits the ברייתא to a mix-up after the blood was sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the exemption applies only when the mix-up happened after זריקה. If it happened before זריקה, all five must bring פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This was taught only when the hides got mixed up after the blood was sprinkled. When the blood was sprinkled, each lamb was at least fit to be eaten. But if they got mixed up before the sprinkling, they must bring פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי applies his rule to the ברייתא. Whether the owners are exempt depends on when the mix-up happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is whether each good lamb was fit to be eaten at the moment of זריקה. If the mix-up came later, the four good lambs were fit at that moment, so their owners have fulfilled the מצוה. If the mix-up came first, every lamb was already in doubt at זריקה, so none of them counts.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in a case where... (a limiting phrase)
At the time the blood was sprinkled

steps.whyThisMatters: This repeats the same rule from Steps 20-21. The status of a קרבן is judged at the moment of זריקה. This is the very rule the next lines debate: does it reach the משנה too, or only the ברייתא?

phrases.english: Abaye said: They only taught this
phrases.notes: The attribution is merged into the statement it introduces.

phrases.english: where they got mixed up after the sprinkling,
because at the time the blood was sprinkled
it was at least fit to be eaten.
phrases.notes: This refers to each of the four good lambs.

phrases.english: But if they got mixed up before the sprinkling —
they are obligated to do the second Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ לְאַחַר זְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי limits the exemption in the ברייתא quoted in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mix-up after זריקה means exempt from פסח שני. A mix-up before זריקה means they must bring פסח שני.

steps.title: If the rule applies to the משנה, it surely applies to the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Whoever places אביי's rule on the משנה would surely apply it to the ברייתא as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever teaches it on the משנה would apply it all the more so to the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins comparing the two versions of where אביי said his rule. This first half explains the version that puts it on the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the animals were perfectly fine; only the people forgot which animal was whose. In the ברייתא, one animal really has a blemish. If a mix-up before זריקה causes a problem even for good animals, it surely causes a problem for animals where one is truly blemished.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on our Mishnah,
phrases.notes: This means the משנה about the slave and master who forgot.

phrases.english: all the more so on the baraita.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי אַמַּתְנִיתִין, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַבָּרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions of אביי's statement, starting with the one about the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If אביי's limit applies to the משנה, where the animals were fine, it surely applies to the ברייתא, where one animal is truly blemished.

steps.title: If the rule was said on the ברייתא, the משנה may be different
steps.stepSummary: Whoever places אביי's rule on the ברייתא would not apply it to the משנה. There the animals are truly fit, and Heaven knows which one belongs to whom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever teaches it on the ברייתא would say it does not apply to the משנה. Since those animals are fit, and if the slave remembers they could be eaten, it is known before Heaven which one belongs to whom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes comparing the two versions. In this version, אביי's limit is only about the ברייתא, so in the משנה the owners would be exempt even if they forgot before זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, nothing is wrong with the animals; the only problem is that the people forgot. If the slave remembers, the animals are fully fit to eat, and Heaven already knows which belongs to whom. Forgetting therefore does not make the קרבן unfit, unlike the ברייתא, where one animal has a real blemish.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of אביי's rule. On the משנה version, it applies to both sources. On the ברייתא version, it applies only to the ברייתא. In the משנה, mere forgetting does not hurt the קרבן, because Heaven knows the truth.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "we don't know" with "the animal is unfit." In the משנה, only the people's knowledge is missing. In the ברייתא, one animal is truly blemished.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the baraita,
but on our Mishnah — no.
phrases.notes: In the משנה they are exempt even if they forgot before זריקה.

phrases.english: Since they are fit,
for if he were to remember, they would be fit to be eaten,
phrases.notes: "He" means the slave, who could remember which animal his master asked for.

phrases.english: it is revealed before Heaven.
phrases.notes: God knows which animal belongs to whom, so the קרבן is not unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי אַבָּרַיְיתָא, אֲבָל אַמַּתְנִיתִין לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the comparison of the two versions by giving the second side.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Not knowing which animal belongs to whom, when the animals themselves are fit, does not make the קרבן unfit. A real blemish does.

steps.title: Questioning the ברייתא: one owner never fulfilled the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא. It asks how all five can be exempt from פסח שני when one of them brought a blemished lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: They are exempt from doing פסח שני. But there is one who did not fulfill his obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא and challenges its ruling. This sets up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with אביי's limit, one lamb really was blemished at זריקה. Its owner never brought a fit קרבן פסח. So how can the ברייתא say that all five are exempt?

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (a formula for quoting a source again in order to discuss it)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: וּפְטוּרִין מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי.
phrases.english: The Master said: And they are exempt from doing the second Pesach.
phrases.notes: This re-quotes the ברייתא from Step 22.

phrases.english: But there is one who did not fulfill his obligation!
phrases.notes: This is the owner of the blemished lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וּפְטוּרִין מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי. וְהָא אִיכָּא חַד דְּלָא נָפֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the comparison of versions and challenges the ruling of the ברייתא itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that all five owners are exempt from פסח שני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One lamb was truly blemished, so its owner never fulfilled the מצוה and should have to bring פסח שני. A blanket exemption for all five does not seem to fit.

steps.title: They are exempt because there is no way to fix it: separate lambs fail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that all five are exempt because nothing workable can be done. If each brings his own פסח, four of them would be bringing חולין into the עזרה, since they already fulfilled their obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is not possible. What should he do? Let each one bring a פסח? Then he would be bringing unconsecrated animals into the Temple courtyard, since four of them already did their פסח properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 26. All five are exempt because there is no practical way to fix the situation, and it begins showing why the first possible fix fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one of the five owners still has a פסח obligation, but nobody knows which one. If all five bring a new פסח, the four who already fulfilled their duty cannot make a real פסח, so their animals stay חולין. Bringing חולין into the עזרה is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Unconsecrated animals brought into the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
They have already performed it (fulfilled the פסח)

steps.confusionAlert: The exemption does not mean the blemished-lamb owner actually fulfilled his פסח. It means there is no way to make him bring a new one without causing a different problem.

phrases.english: Because it is not possible.
What should he do?
Let each and every one bring a Pesach offering?
He would be bringing unconsecrated animals into the Temple courtyard,
since four of them have already performed it.
phrases.notes: The four owners of unblemished lambs already fulfilled their obligation and cannot consecrate a new פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אִיפְשָׁר. הֵיכִי לֶיעְבֵּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 26 by showing that no practical fix exists.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical impossibility: the exemption exists because any fix would create a new violation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since one owner brought a blemished lamb, all five should have to bring פסח שני
steps.terutzMaskana: They are exempt because separate new offerings would mean bringing חולין into the עזרה

steps.title: A single shared lamb also fails: eaten by the unregistered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second option, that all five bring one shared פסח. That lamb would be eaten by people who cannot be properly registered for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let all of them bring one פסח together? Then the פסח would be eaten by people who are not registered for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its answer by testing a second possible fix and showing that it also fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח may only be eaten by people registered (מנויים) for it. The four who already fulfilled their obligation cannot join a group for a new פסח, so they would be eating it without being registered.

keyTerms.meaning: Let all of them bring one shared פסח
By those not registered for it

phrases.english: Let all of them bring one Pesach offering?
It would turn out that the Pesach is eaten
by those not registered for it.
phrases.notes: Someone who already fulfilled his obligation cannot be registered for another פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַיְתֵי כּוּלְּהוּ חַד פֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer of Step 27 by rejecting the second possible fix.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical impossibility, second option ruled out
steps.terutzMaskana: A shared פסח would be eaten by unregistered people, so it is not a valid solution either

steps.title: Why not use a conditional offering: פסח or שלמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that there is no fix. Each owner could bring an animal with a condition: if his original lamb was the blemished one, this is a פסח, and if not, it is a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of answer is this? Let each one bring his פסח and say: If mine was the blemished one, this animal I bring now is a פסח. If mine was unblemished, this animal I bring now is a שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer by proposing a clever fix that seems to avoid both problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A conditional (תנאי) seems to solve everything. The one real obligated owner gets a valid פסח, and the other four bring a valid שלמים instead of חולין. If this works, the claim that "it is not possible" falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? (a phrase that rejects the previous reasoning)
And let him stipulate (make a condition)

phrases.english: What is this?
Let each one of them bring his Pesach offering,
and stipulate and say:
If mine was the blemished one,
this one that I am bringing now shall be a Pesach offering,
and if mine was unblemished,
this one that I am bringing now shall be a peace-offering!
phrases.notes: Leftover פסח animals can become שלמים, so the condition seems workable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Steps 27–28 by proposing a fix that seems to avoid both problems.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that it is impossible to fix the situation (משום דלא איפשר)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A conditional offering avoids both problems: the four would not be bringing חולין, and nobody would eat a פסח without being registered.

steps.title: The conditional offering is also not possible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: the conditional offering does not work either. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to reject the conditional-offering idea. This line sets up the explanation, which comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא holds firm that the conditional approach fails. It has not yet said why, so this step only opens the answer.

phrases.english: It is not possible,
phrases.notes: The reason continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge of Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical impossibility (explanation follows on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A conditional פסח/שלמים offering would solve the problem
steps.terutzMaskana: The conditional offering is also not workable; the reason follows
